chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Abdullah ibn Latif al-Taflisi, from Razin, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was struck with the sword, his head fell, then they began to cut off his head. A caller called out from the middle of the Throne: 'Indeed! O you confused community, the strayed ones after their Prophet! May Allah not grant you success for Eid al-Adha nor for Eid al-Fitr.'

He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So, by Allah, there is no doubt that they were not granted success, nor will they be granted success until the avenger of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) takes revenge.'

key_terms.فِطْرٍ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: What did the caller from the Throne say about the community after the death of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the divine judgment on the Umayyad community following the martyrdom of Imam Al-Husayn (AS), linking their spiritual failure to the delay in Qa'im al-Husayn's appearance. The proclamation from beneath the Throne emphasizes that their ritual successes in Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr were hollow until the avenger of his blood arose, a concept central to Shia eschatology regarding the Mahdi.
